issues.body:
This line turns bytes-ingest on for the PUBLISHED @jeswr/sparq bundle, yet a grep for 'bytes-ingest' across .github/workflows/ returns zero hits. Concretely:

- ci.yml adds an explicit wasm32 `cargo build` + `cargo clippy -D warnings` leg for every other opt-in sparq-wasm feature (shacl ~line 900, jsonld ~908/912, policy ~919, explain-json ~928). bytes-ingest has none.
- ci.yml runs `wasm-pack test --node` with `--features shacl` (line 1005) and `--features jsonld` (line 1011) and `--features explain-json` (line 1029). There is no `--features bytes-ingest` leg, so the `#[cfg(feature = "bytes-ingest")]` block in crates/sparq-wasm/tests/web.rs (line 930) never runs.
- The workspace test shards archive with `--features approx-ann,filtered-ann,vec-predicate` (ci.yml:419), NOT --all-features, so the native `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in crates/sparq-wasm/src/bytes.rs is never compiled into a running test binary either. (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` at ci.yml:1166 type-checks it, but does not run it.)

Net effect: of the three test suites written for this feature, only the JS-level one (js/test/store.test.mjs, via the gating `js` lane, which does build with bytes-ingest) actually executes in CI. That covers the happy path. The fail-closed invalid-UTF-8 rejection — the security-relevant arm, which bytes.rs:100-104 explicitly says is asserted in the wasm32 web.rs 'under the bytes-ingest feature' — is asserted by a test that no CI job ever reaches.

Rated minor, not major: decode_utf8 is a three-line `std::str::from_utf8` wrapper that is correct by construction, and a compile break would still be caught by the all-features clippy pass and by the `js` lane's build:wasm. The gap is test wiring and gate coverage, not observed behaviour.
issues.fix_hint:
Mirror the pattern the other opt-in features already use in .github/workflows/ci.yml, next to the explain-json legs:

  - name: Build sparq-wasm for the browser target (bytes-ingest feature)
    run: cargo build -p sparq-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features bytes-ingest
  - name: clippy (wasm32 target, bytes-ingest feature, deny warnings)
    run: cargo clippy -p sparq-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets --features bytes-ingest -- -D warnings

and, beside the shacl/jsonld/explain-json headless legs:

  - name: Headless wasm tests (wasm-pack test --node, bytes-ingest feature)
    working-directory: crates/sparq-wasm
    run: wasm-pack test --node --features bytes-ingest

That last one is the important one — it is what actually executes tests/web.rs::load_bytes_invalid_utf8_fails_closed and the native bytes.rs unit tests. Since ci.yml is outside this diff, filing it as a follow-up bead is also acceptable, but it should not be dropped: the feature is in the published bundle.
issues.title: build:wasm ships bytes-ingest in the published bundle, but no CI leg builds, clippies, or TESTS that feature — the Rust tests for it never execute

issues.body:
The added test is non-vacuous for what it checks (DATA parses to 6 triples per the adjacent 'fromString parses and deduplicates' test, so a silently-empty fromBytes store would fail the size comparison, and the queryJson string comparison is a genuine result-equivalence check). Two gaps:

1. It asserts `fromBytes.size === fromString.size` rather than an absolute count. That is a relative assertion; it is only load-bearing because the string path is independently pinned at 6 one test above. An absolute `assert.equal(fromBytes.size, 6)` would make it self-standing.
2. Neither the fail-closed invalid-UTF-8 arm nor the `options.baseIri` -> loadBytesWithBase branch is exercised at the JS level. Given the minor above (the Rust tests that do cover those never run in CI), the JS lane is currently the ONLY executed coverage of this feature, so those two arms are effectively untested end to end.
issues.title: The JS bytes-ingest test covers only the happy path — no invalid-UTF-8 and no baseIri assertion

issues.body:
1. `share(rawMs, wrappedMs)` returns `Math.max(0, (wrappedMs - rawMs) / wrappedMs)`. If a wrapped path ever measures FASTER than the queryJson baseline — entirely possible in a single-process bench with no isolation, and the exact signal that the measurement is noise-dominated — the reported wrapper_share is a clean-looking 0.0 rather than something that flags 'this run is not meaningful'. The advisory:true / canonical:false labelling and the note already keep the output honest overall, so this is a nit, not a correctness or honesty defect.

2. `measure()` (lines 49-58) is `bench()` (lines 38-47) with the console.log swapped for a return value. Two near-identical warm-up-then-best-of-N loops now coexist in one 150-line script.

Methodology itself checks out: queryBindingsStream and queryJson both run off the same wasm SPARQL-JSON chunk cursor (js/src/store.ts:384-399 vs the chunk path behind queryJson), so queryJson is a legitimate raw baseline and wrapper_share really does isolate the JS parse/materialise overhead.
issues.title: share() clamps a negative share to 0, hiding the anomaly it would signal; measure() duplicates bench()

verdict.summary: Round 5 fixes BOTH round-4 findings; nothing blocking remains. (1) The carried major is genuinely resolved: consumeResultStream() no longer uses `for await` and instead drains the stream through its real contract — stream.on('data')/.on('end')/.on('error'). I verified this against js/src/result-stream.ts: on() returns `this` (line 51-59) so the chain is valid; adding the 'data' listener calls resume() -> #schedulePump(), which defers the first pull to queueMicrotask (line 191-214), while the Promise executor runs synchronously — so 'end' (#end, line 238) and 'error' (#fail, line 245) are both attached before any row is emitted. Empty results resolve(0) via the done->#end path; a terminal failure rejects via 'error' with no following 'end', so the promise settles exactly once. (2) The nit is resolved: fromBytes now typeof-guards WasmStore.loadBytes/loadBytesWithBase and throws a clear 'requires a wasm bundle built with the bytes-ingest feature' error instead of an opaque TypeError on the lean bundle. PUBLISHED PACKAGE (still correct): fromBytes delegates to the opt-in feature-gated bindings in crates/sparq-wasm/src/bytes.rs, which fail-closed-validate UTF-8 (std::str::from_utf8 -> JsError, never a panic or lossy decode) and then reuse the EXISTING Graph::load_str / load_str_with_base path, so the store is byte-identical to string ingest. Zero new deps; bytes-ingest is OFF by default (module declared at end-of-lib.rs so the lean bundle stays byte-identical); build:wasm enables it; the tracked sparq-client .d.ts and SKILL.md are synced, and the added .d.ts entries are in wasm-bindgen's alphabetical order. The JS test is non-vacuous (a silently-empty fromBytes store fails the size comparison against the string store, which the adjacent test pins at 6, and queryJson equality is a real result-equivalence check).
